newsitem.title: UK: Sales of OTC healthcare products up 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Sales of OTC healthcare products up 30 pct.

text.p: Worldwide sales of over-the-counter healthcare products rose 30 percent from 1991 through 1995 and are expected to rise a further 21 percent to $64 billion by 2000, according to a report released on Wednesday.

"By far the most dramatic growth will occur in the developing regions of East and South Asia, where OTC sales are expected to double, driven by expansion in India and China," Euromonitor, a market research group, said in its report, "The World Market for OTC Healthcare".

Worldwide retail sales of OTC healthcare products totalled $53 billion in 1995. Vitamins and dietary supplements constituted the largest segment at 19.4 percent, followed by cough and cold remedies at 17.2 percent and medicated skin care at 17.1 percent, Euromonitor reported.

Vitamins and dietary supplements are forecast to continue to account for the largest percentage of sales, rising 21 percent to $13 billion in 2000 from $10 billion in 1995. But medicated skin care is expected to post the fastest growth, rising 23 percent to $11 billion in 2000, Euromonitor said.

The study found that Americans are the top spenders for OTC healthcare products, spending an average of $70.42 per person. They are closely followed by the Germans at an average of $69.14 per person and the Danes at $69.08. At the other end of the scale, the Japanese spend an average of $36.20 each, with Swedes spending $36.63 each and the French spending $37.50 each, the study found.
